newsitem.title: FRANCE: Reuters French Advertising & Media Digest - May 12.
newsitem.headline: Reuters French Advertising & Media Digest - May 12.

text.p: REUTERS FRENCH ADVERTISING & MEDIA DIGEST
News from Reuters and the French press on Advertising, Marketing, Media, the Internet, Brand-name products and People News.
ADVERTISING & MARKETING:

PARIS - French oil, chemicals and healthcare company Elf Aquitaine says it is launching press advertising campaign that seeks to give a human face to the firm, usually identified with the petrol pump. (Reuter).

PARIS - Michele-Bleustein-Blanchet, the youngest daughter of the founder of French advertising agency Publicis, is trying to sell her Publicis stake, while Elisabeth Badinter, his second daughter, is trying to prevent the sale. (La Tribune)

PARIS - French private television station TF1 saw a small rise in its overall audience in April compared to March, while public station France 3 showed a fall, according to audience measurement body Mediametrie's monthly Mediamat study. (Reuter)
MEDIA & THE INTERNET:

PARIS - Canal Plus finalises a new deal under which it will reserve 75 percent of its purchases of French films for a first television showing from independent producers from the year 2000. (Les Echos).

PARIS - Television station M6 says its turnover rose to 692 million francs ($121.8 million) in the first quarter of 1997 from 521 million in 1996's first quarter. Advertising revenues rose 12.4 percent in the period. (Reuter)

PARIS - Turnover at television staion TF1 was 2.41 billion francs in the first quarter of 1997, up from 2.28 billion in 1996's first quarter, the company says. Advertising revenue rose 2.3 percent in the first quarter. (Reuter)
BRAND-NAME PRODUCTS & MARKETS:

LONDON - Bernard Arnault, chairman of French luxury goods and drinks group LVMH Moet Hennessy and a non-executive director of Guinness, votes against the proposed merger of Grand Metropolitan and Guinness. (Reuter)

PARIS - French Agriculture Minister Philippe Vassesur threatens to ban imports of U.S. meat treated with hormones, even if it meant heavy fines for Paris. France would also require special labels on American meat from July 1, he says. (Reuter)
TURIN - The European new car market rose 9.2 percent to 1,258,200 units in April, helped by a large rise in Italian new car regisrations, the Italian vehicle makers' association Anfia says. (Reuter)
PEOPLE NEWS: PARIS - Michel-Hubert Jamard has been appointed as communications director for OTV, the water treatment subsidiary of Compagnie Generale des Eaux. (La Tribune)
PARIS - Michel Agopian has been appointed managing director, operations at 3Com France with a mission to promote and develop sales of systems to big companies. (La Tribune)
Paris Editorial, Sue Landau
